messages.content: New one: Denver WaterTech conference. Exhibitor assignment came through for Nov 17-20 at the convention center. Badge pickup is Monday at noon, booth setup Monday afternoon, and I’m on an early Tuesday panel. I need Bay Area-DEN flight options plus hotel choices. Sunday afternoon arrival if the extra night gets approved; Monday morning only if it is genuinely low-risk. Don’t book yet.
Understood. Before I shortlist it: are you assuming downtown only, and do you need to stay through Thursday teardown?

Downtown only. Teardown is the open question. Show closes Thursday afternoon but I don’t know crate timing yet. For now show Sunday through Thursday hotel nights if cancellable, and flag whether Wednesday night return is a bad idea.
Any hotel rate ceiling or company rule about using the official block?
Target under $300 before taxes. Official block is preferred if it’s not worse. I want good guest feedback, breakfast or coffee easy, dinner nearby, and the room basics visible.
Which Bay Area airports should I compare?
SFO and OAK. SJC only if it is clearly better. And one connection max, though Denver should be nonstop.

Flight shortlist: best fit if Sunday is approved is United SFO-DEN Sun Nov 16, 2:05-5:38 p.m., nonstop, about $286 economy. It protects Monday setup and gets you downtown before dinner. Lower-cost backup is Southwest OAK-DEN, 3:25-6:55 p.m., nonstop, about $214 before any EarlyBird/boarding add-on; cheaper but less convenient if you are starting from San Francisco and seats are not assigned. Monday fallback is United SFO-DEN, 6:15-9:46 a.m.; it can work on paper, but a delay, bag wait, or downtown traffic would eat the cushion before noon badge pickup. I would not use a mid-morning Monday departure.
Can you include a later Sunday option? I may have something Sunday morning.

Later protected option: United SFO-DEN Sun 5:20-8:52 p.m., nonstop, about $312. Still acceptable because Monday morning remains open, but you would reach the hotel closer to 10 p.m. The 2:05 flight is cleaner if the afternoon is free.
Hotel side?

Three worth comparing. Official block: Hyatt Regency Denver at Colorado Convention Center, about $289, 2-minute walk, 4.4 Google rating, on-site restaurant/market, rooms list a coffeemaker and mini-fridge. It is the easiest for booth runs. Nearby higher-rated option: The Slate Denver, about $263, 6-minute walk, 4.5 Google rating, on-site restaurant/bar and easier nearby breakfast spots; king rooms list coffeemaker and mini-fridge. Third option: Embassy Suites Downtown, about $279, 4.3 rating, included breakfast and suite fridge, but it tends to be busier and less business-focused during events.
Any official block room cheaper that isn’t a commute?

The cheapest block-adjacent one I see is Hilton Garden Inn Union Station at about $239, 4.3 rating, good restaurant access and room fridge/coffee, but it is a 20-25 minute walk or short rideshare. I would call that an acceptable backup, not a best fit, because random booth runs would be annoying.
Skip Union Station. I need quick access back to the booth.

Then the real hotel decision is Hyatt Regency versus The Slate. Hyatt is simplest for expo logistics and official-block optics. The Slate has slightly better guest feedback and better breakfast/dinner flexibility, but it is a short walk with any booth materials.
What about return timing? I’ll probably have customer dinners Tuesday and maybe Wednesday.

I would avoid a Wednesday night return unless that reception disappears. For Thursday, use two placeholders: United DEN-SFO 3:35-5:20 p.m. if teardown release is before about 1 p.m.; safer United DEN-SFO 6:45-8:32 p.m. if the show closes at 2 and crate paperwork drags. Southwest into OAK around 5:10-6:55 p.m. is cheaper, but it is less useful if your outbound is from SFO.
Could the Monday fallback be from OAK instead?

OAK has a Southwest nonstop around 7:00-10:30 a.m. Monday. It is better than a later morning flight, but still leaves little room for any delay, the airport-to-downtown transfer, and badge pickup. I would keep it only as the company-denies-Sunday backup.
Make this forwardable with the ask-before-booking items. Ops is deciding on the extra night.
One last point: rental car or no rental? For a convention-center trip, rideshare or rail is usually simpler unless a customer site visit gets added.
No rental unless someone adds a site visit. Rideshare is fine. Keep both Sunday SFO options in the note.

Forwardable Denver shortlist: best fit if Sunday night is approved is United SFO-DEN Sun Nov 16, 2:05-5:38 p.m. nonstop, rideshare downtown, and either Hyatt Regency Convention Center or The Slate Denver for Sun-Thu on a cancellable rate. Later Sunday SFO option is United 5:20-8:52 p.m.; acceptable if Sunday morning is blocked, but it makes the arrival night later. Monday fallback only if Sunday is denied: United SFO-DEN 6:15-9:46 a.m. is the least risky Monday option, while OAK 7:00-10:30 a.m. is cheaper but tighter. Hotel trade-off: Hyatt Regency is the easiest official-block booth hotel; The Slate is the better-rated nearby business option with stronger dining/breakfast convenience. I would skip Union Station because booth access matters. Return: avoid Wednesday night for now; hold Thursday afternoon versus evening until teardown timing is confirmed. Ask before booking: Sunday-night approval, Hyatt block versus The Slate, and whether Thursday teardown allows an afternoon return or requires the safer evening flight.

The Slate: about $263, 6-minute walk, 4.5 rating, better nearby breakfast and dinner choices, king room lists coffeemaker and mini-fridge. Hyatt wins on booth convenience; Slate wins on guest feedback and food logistics.
Reception is at the convention center, not the Hyatt. Breakfast before the Tuesday panel matters more than being in the block. Is Slate quick enough?

Yes. Slate has on-site breakfast options and nearby coffee, then about a 6-minute walk to the convention center. For the Tuesday panel, it is still easy. I would just verify the king room fridge/coffee listing at booking.
Then Slate unless cancellation is worse.
Cancellation is comparable: both show cancellable until roughly 72 hours before arrival. No major penalty difference.
Return timing?

Use two Thursday return candidates. If teardown release is firm by about 2:30 p.m., United DEN-SFO 5:05-6:50 p.m. is workable. If crate paperwork can slip, United DEN-SFO 7:40-9:25 p.m. is safer. Hotel pick is The Slate Denver over the Hyatt block because the reception is at the convention center, breakfast matters before the Tuesday panel, and cancellation is similar; verify king-room coffeemaker and mini-fridge at booking. Return remains open: choose United DEN-SFO Thu 5:05-6:50 p.m. only if teardown release by about 2:30 is confirmed; otherwise use the safer 7:40-9:25 p.m. flight. No booking yet.
